name: East Shoreham Covered Railroad Bridge
facts: East Shoreham Covered Railroad Bridge, built in 1897 by the Rutland Railroad Company, is Vermont’s only surviving wooden Howe truss railroad bridge, spanning 109 feet across the Lemon Fair River.
The bridge’s 20‑foot width and 13.5‑foot internal clearance once carried the Addison Branch line until 1951, after which the tracks were removed and the structure preserved as a historic landmark.
Listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1974, the bridge’s stone abutments faced in concrete and vertical board siding protect its original wooden trusses and iron rod verticals.
